One action inside a workflow. v2 types: Start, Collect, Check, Suggest, Pre-flight, Ask a person (approval gate), Act, Verify, Escalate, File evidence.
A repeatable sequence of steps an agent runs, mapped to framework requirements it produces evidence for. One run counts toward every requirement it maps to, at the relation strength stated.
The order a framework is worked through, requirement by requirement, with the workflows that cover each. Gaps are shown, not hidden.

v1 was generated from apps/backend/src/api/routers/pack_catalogue.py. v2 is a proposal; nothing here is in code yet.
New. Before any external write: dry run, blast radius, rollback path, confirm credentials are scoped to this change only.
New. After an external write: re-read target state, confirm only approved changes applied; on mismatch roll back and escalate.
New. On approval SLA breach: notify delegate or manager; run stays paused; nothing is recorded or changed (deny by default).
Outcomes in v2: approve, approve with edits, request changes, reject, accept risk as-is (justification required). Rejections still file evidence.
Agent does nothing unless asked for a draft.
Agent collects and checks; humans write every conclusion (used where independence matters, e.g. internal audit).
Agent proposes; nothing is recorded or changed until a human approves. v1 default.
Agent files records inside FairMind without approval; humans review by sampling and on escalation. Never external writes.
Agent executes a pre-approved playbook action without per-run approval (e.g. incident containment). Every A4 action is logged and reviewed after.
The workflow's output is the primary evidence for the whole requirement. Use sparingly; auditors decide sufficiency.
Covers a material part of the requirement; other evidence is needed for the rest.
Contributes evidence; not sufficient on its own.

Changes_v2.3: Added workflows for threats v2.2 left uncovered: AI red teaming, deepfake and impersonation defence, LLM output handling, inter-agent trust, agent runaway containment, data and model retention and disposal
Added 48 evaluations (OWASP LLM, Agentic and MCP gaps, ATLAS tactics, adversarial ML, offensive AI and content safety, data, privacy, fairness drift, use-case suites)
109 evaluations: 10 engine exists, 24 partial, 75 not found
Mapped every evaluation to exact requirement IDs ('Tests' relation), so a passing result counts as evidence for that requirement
Added a 'Tested' coverage state (a requirement no workflow satisfies but an evaluation tests) and counted it in the coverage percentage
Split into granular patterns: every workflow and evaluation sits in exactly one; every pattern in exactly one pack
Rebuilt journeys for every framework with 5 or more active requirements, counting coverage by workflows and by tests separately

Added customer bundles (GenAI copilot, agentic automation, high-risk decisions, ISO/IEC 42001, EU AI Act provider, NIST AI RMF, India financial services, AI security baseline) with coverage of their target frameworks
Changes_v2.2: Tagged frameworks, workflows and evaluations with a pillar (Govern, Evaluate, Secure, Comply) and workflows and evaluations with a pattern

Added 19 FairMind patterns across the four pillars (structure modelled on OSA's control-bundle patterns; names and content are FairMind's own). Every workflow and evaluation sits in exactly one pattern
Added Pack_Library: 14 installable packs built from patterns. The v2 'Packs' sheet (one pack per framework) is kept for reference; frameworks are now journeys, not packs
Added Journey_Builder (pack-by-pack cumulative coverage per framework) and Journey_Summary (coverage with all packs, supported-only and gaps)
Renamed the v2 Packs sheet to Packs_v2 and marked it superseded
Pillars: Run the AI management system: policies, accountability, inventory, risk and impact, data and suppliers, and the metrics that show systems are under control.
Test systems before and after release: quality, fairness and bias (FairMind's core engines), agent behaviour and production drift.

Protect LLM applications and agents against the OWASP, MITRE ATLAS and NIST adversarial threat classes, secure the AI supply chain, defend against offensive AI and deepfakes, and respond to incidents.
Meet specific legal and certification obligations (EU AI Act, ISO/IEC 42001, AIUC-1 and others) and show it, through journeys that add packs up to each framework.

Findings: ISO/IEC 42001 journey covers 4 of 27 clause-level requirements (5.2, 6.1.2, 6.1.4 and 8.2 as support) and 2 of 38 Annex A controls (A.2.2, A.5.2). 'Coming soon: 5' hides about 20 sub-requirements.
Track journeys at sub-clause and Annex A level. v2 maps every clause and every Annex A control; see Coverage_Summary.
AI policy review omits A.2.4 'Review of the AI policy', the control the workflow literally performs, and A.2.3 alignment with other policies.
Add A.2.4 as Satisfies, A.2.3 as Partial. Add publish and acknowledgement so 5.2's 'communicated' part is evidenced.
AI risk assessment proposes treatments but maps no treatment requirement (6.1.3, 8.3) and produces no Statement of Applicability. Auditors trace risk to SoA to control.
Split treatment into ai_risk_treatment_soa (6.1.3, 8.3, SoA) and residual_risk_acceptance (explicit, time-bound).
Impact assessment description already covers individuals, groups and society but maps only 6.1.4 and A.5.2. 8.4, A.5.3, A.5.4, A.5.5 are left on the table.
Add them; use ISO/IEC 42005 as method; emit FRIA content when EU Art 27 or Korea impact assessment applies.

Access control review marks all six mappings 'Satisfies'. A periodic access review is one piece of evidence for CC6.1-6.3 and A.5.15 / A.8.2, not their satisfaction. CC6.1 covers logical access architecture as a whole.
v2 removes these frameworks (see F19). The lesson stands: use Satisfies only where the output is the primary evidence (e.g. AIUC-1 B007) and require rationale per mapping.
Mappings go straight from workflow to framework requirement. With 15+ frameworks every workflow change means N re-mappings, and 'one run counts toward every framework' becomes unmaintainable.
Insert a common control layer (FairMind control objectives) between workflows and frameworks. Workflows evidence controls; controls map to requirements; crosswalk work happens once.
Ask step has two outcomes (approved, changes asked). No reject, accept-as-is, delegate, or timeout path; the revise loop is unbounded.
Five outcomes, max 3 revise rounds, Escalate step on SLA breach, deny by default when approvers are unreachable (SG MGF 2.2.2).
Nothing stops the requester approving their own run, or an owner approving changes to their own access.
Add SoD rule per workflow (Workflows sheet). Enforce in code, not policy text.
Access review 'Act' writes to Okta and AWS IAM with no dry run, blast-radius check, verification or rollback. This is OWASP ASI02/ASI03 exposure for FairMind's own agent.
Pre-flight and Verify steps around every external write, per-run scoped credentials, dual approval for privileged changes. Consider deferring external writes to v2 except one showcase.
'Files the evidence' is undefined: no schema, period, population, hash, signer, or agent trace. Auditors need population and period to sample.
Define an evidence schema (see Questions G) including model version, prompt template version and tool-call trace for every agent-produced item.
FairMind's agent is itself an AI system in the customer's AIMS (and in scope if FairMind seeks 42001 or AIUC-1). Nothing in v1 governs it.
Add fairmind_assurance pack and Agentic_Runtime controls. This is also a sales point: the governance tool governs itself in the open.
Triggers are only 'requested' or 'due'. The value of an agentic GRC tool is reacting to events: model version change, new MCP server, leaver, drift alert, regulatory update.
Event triggers per workflow (Workflows sheet). Pick the v1 event sources (Questions D).
Lifecycle stages are only Govern and Assess; access review is labelled Govern though it is an operating control.
Use the 12-stage list in Overview; align to NIST functions and 42001 A.6 lifecycle.
'Systems' mixes external connectors (Okta, AWS IAM, HRIS) with internal modules (Policy library, AI system inventory). No fallback when a connector is missing.
Split into connector vs internal object; declare required vs optional; manual upload fallback labelled as lower-assurance evidence.
No run scope. Policy is org-level, risk and impact are per system, access is per system. 200 systems means 200 runs and 200 approvals.
Add run scope and fan-out rules; batch approval UX for per-system workflows.
Pack and workflow 'Version 1' with no rule for in-flight runs or framework version pinning. AIUC-1 releases quarterly; customers certify against one version per year.
Pin framework version per customer; in-flight runs finish on their start version; migration notes per version.
Journey order has no dependencies. Inventory must precede risk; impact before residual acceptance; evals before release.
Risk assessment assumes criteria and appetite exist. No workflow establishes them (6.1.1, 6.1.2 inputs).
Add criteria and appetite setup to aims_context_scope or a dedicated setup workflow.
v1 ships a general security pack (ISO 27001 / SOC 2) inside an AI governance product. AIUC-1 explicitly leaves non-AI risks to SOC 2, ISO 27001 and GDPR; FairMind should too.

security_controls pack removed. Access review re-homed to AIUC-1 and remapped to AI requirements (B007, B006, SG MGF 2.1.2-ID). General security and privacy frameworks listed in Out_of_scope with their hand-off.

No coverage of agent-specific requirements: identity, permission bounding, tool-call testing, oversight effectiveness, kill switch. These are the core of AIUC-1 (B006, D003), SG MGF and OWASP Agentic.
Shipping framework text is a legal risk: ISO is copyrighted, AIUC-1 is all rights reserved, OWASP is CC BY-SA (share-alike).
IDs plus FairMind paraphrase only; licence column in Frameworks.

Ask the Head of AI governance

Sends Head of AI governance a decision card for AIMS context and scope: what would change, why, the risk if approved, the agent's confidence band and links to the evidence. Gate: Approve / approve with edits / request changes (max 3 rounds) / reject. SoD: Approver is not the run initiator
record (approved / approved with edits); revise (changes asked: max 3 rounds then escalate); file-evidence (rejected: reasons recorded); escalate (no decision by SLA)
Approver unreachable: deny by default, nothing recorded or changed

Saves the approved context register and scope statement as a new controlled version.
Write fails: stop, no partial changes, escalate
Reworks the proposal using the approver's comments. Maximum 3 rounds, then escalates.
Notifies the approver's delegate or manager; run stays paused; nothing is recorded or changed.
No delegate: notify Head of AI governance

Collected content is data, never instructions

Missing or ambiguous input produces an explicit 'cannot conclude' with what is needed.
Deterministic checks (dates, presence, thresholds, SoD) run before LLM judgement; LLM handles unstructured reading only.
Pre-flight and verify around external writes
Dry run, blast radius, rollback plan before; state re-read after; auto rollback on mismatch.
If an approver is unreachable or no policy covers the action, nothing is recorded or changed.
Short, risk stated, diff view, confidence band, link to evidence; long logs only on expand.

Redact or tokenise personal data before model calls where the task allows.

Questions: My default if you do not decide
Fill column G (yellow). Defaults in column E apply if left blank.
Who is the first buyer: AI product companies seeking ISO 42001 / AIUC-1 (providers), enterprises adopting agents (deployers), or regulated BFSI in India / Singapore?
Pack order, default autonomy, and which external writes matter all change with the buyer.
AI product companies chasing 42001 + AIUC-1: certification gives a deadline and a budget.
Is FairMind (open source) the engine and Axonome AI governance the commercial product on top, or one codebase?
Decides what lives in the public pack_catalogue.py and what stays in a private content repo.
OSS engine + schema + sample packs; commercial content packs and connectors.
Stakflo already has an AI/ML inventory, AI policy checklist, HITRUST AI mapping and a 297-control library. Will any of it be reused here, and who owns it (SQ1 or Axonome)?
Content provenance and IP ownership need a written answer before anything is copied across.
Build FairMind content independently; no reuse until ownership is agreed in writing.
Is FairMind AI-governance only, or also general GRC (full ISO 27001 / SOC 2)?
The security overlay pack drifts toward Vanta / Drata territory; that is a different product.
Decided 1 Nov 2026: AI governance only. ISO 27001, SOC 2, GDPR, DPDP, CCPA ADMT out of scope (see Out_of_scope).
Does each AI system carry a declared value-chain role (provider, deployer, both, importer) that switches which workflows activate?
EU AI Act and SG MGF allocate duties by role; without it, customers get irrelevant tasks.
Yes, set in regulatory_applicability, legal sign-off.
Adopt a common control layer between workflows and framework requirements? If yes, author your own, adopt CSA AICM (licence), or SCF?
Without it, 15 frameworks x 50 workflows is unmaintainable (F06).
Own control objectives (~80), each mapped to frameworks; AICM as cross-reference only.
Accept Satisfies / Partially satisfies / Supports semantics? Who can mark Satisfies: content team, customer, or auditor-accepted flag?
Over-claiming is the fastest way to lose auditor trust (F05).
Content team proposes; customer's auditor can accept or downgrade per tenant.
Pin framework versions per customer (AIUC-1 quarterly) the way Drata does, with the new version shown only at the customer's recertification month?
Yes. Show diffs between pinned and latest.
Ship framework text or not? ISO copyrighted, AIUC-1 all rights reserved, OWASP CC BY-SA.
Share-alike can attach to derived content; ISO text is a licence breach.
IDs + FairMind paraphrase; customers can attach licensed text.
Should every mapping carry provenance: author, rationale, source crosswalk (e.g. AIUC-1's published 42001 crosswalk), review date?
Auditors and customers will ask why a mapping exists.
Yes; mapping rows without rationale fail CI.
Measure coverage at requirement level only, or also evidence freshness (age vs required period)?
A control 'covered' by year-old evidence is not covered.
Strict order (later items blocked) or recommended order with dependency warnings?
Strict order frustrates mature customers; no order confuses new ones.
Recommended order; hard prerequisites only at the release gate.
Journey granularity: clause (5 rows) or sub-clause + Annex A (65 rows)?
Auditors work at sub-clause and control level.
Sub-clause + Annex A, grouped visually by clause.
Multi-framework customers: one merged, de-duplicated plan or parallel journeys?
Merged plan by workflow, with per-framework progress bars.
How are exclusions handled (SoA 'not applicable' with justification)?
42001 requires justification for every Annex A exclusion.
Exclusion is a decision record with approver and review date.
Certification-timeline mode: plan backward from a target audit date (42001 Stage 1/2; AIUC-1 audit + quarterly retests)?
Gives the buyer a reason to come back weekly.
Which event sources are in v1: model registry webhook, Git, CI/CD, SIEM, HRIS leaver, agent platform logs, regulatory feed?
Every event trigger needs a connector.
Git, CI/CD, HRIS leaver, model registry, regulatory feed.
Run fan-out: per org, per AI system, per agent? With 200 systems, batch approvals or one by one?
Approval fatigue kills A2 autonomy (SG MGF 2.2.2).
Per system runs, batched approval cards grouped by owner and risk.
Can customers fork and edit workflows? If yes, how do mappings stay valid after edits?
Editable workflows are expected; silent mapping drift is dangerous.
Fork allowed; edited steps drop to 'Supports' until re-reviewed.
Default approval SLA per gate type before Escalate?
3 business days; 4 hours for incident gates.
In-flight runs when a workflow version changes: finish on old version or migrate?
Evidence must match the procedure that produced it.
Auto-chain workflows (risk assessment -> treatment -> residual acceptance) or manual start?
Chaining is the agentic value; uncontrolled chaining creates noise.
Auto-chain with a single 'next steps' approval.
Which gate outcomes ship in v1: approve, approve with edits, request changes, reject, accept risk as-is, delegate, defer?
More outcomes means better evidence and more UI.
First five; delegate and defer later.
A rejection shows the control operated and a human exercised judgement.
Which workflows need dual approval by default, and can customers set thresholds (e.g. residual risk above appetite)?
SoD expectations differ by customer size.
Residual acceptance above appetite, permission bounding, privileged access, release of top-tier agents.
Show the agent's confidence on approval cards as a number or a band?
Numbers invite false precision; bands are easier to calibrate.
Bands (high / medium / low) with the reason.
Require written justification for high-risk approvals?
SG MGF suggests it for high-risk actions; adds friction.
Yes for accept-as-is and high-risk tiers.
Can an approver delegate future approvals of a class to the agent (auto-approve minor changes)?
Moves a workflow from A2 to A3 per class.
Only for change management 'minor' class, with sampled review.
Default autonomy per tenant: A2 everywhere with opt-in A3/A4 per workflow?
Which actions can ever be A4 (no per-run human)?
Only pre-approved incident containment and internal record filing.
External writes (Okta, IAM, agent gateway, CI/CD, LMS) in v1 or later?
Each needs pre-flight, verify, rollback, privileged connector and change windows.
v1: read-only connectors plus one showcase write (CI/CD release token). Others in v2.
Model choice and hosting for FairMind's agent: single provider, BYO model, or open-weight on-prem for regulated buyers?
Affects AIUC-1 E006 due diligence, residency and eval burden.
One provider at launch with BYO-key; open-weight later.
Policy for instruction-like content found in collected evidence: strip, quarantine, or flag?
Vendor questionnaires and tickets are injection vectors (ASI01).
Treat as data, flag in findings, never execute.
Enforce citations in code (finding dropped without valid citation)?
Hallucinated findings are the worst failure for a GRC tool.
No implicit memory; explicit, reviewable knowledge items only.
Who builds and owns golden sets per workflow, and what threshold blocks a model upgrade?
Without them, model upgrades are untested changes to every control.
Content team owns; block below 95% on deterministic checks, human review on the rest.
Evidence schema fields: control refs, period, population, sample, source, collected-at, hash, collector, approver, decision, agent trace refs. Anything to add or drop?
Auditors sample from population and period.
Freshness rules per mapping (e.g. access review 90 days, impact assessment 12 months)?
Per mapping, defaulted from framework cadence.
Immutability: hash chain, WORM storage, or both?
Log immutability is in SG MGF 2.3.3 and expected by auditors.
Hash chain in v1; WORM option for enterprise.
Auditor experience: read-only role, sampling tool, export format (PDF pack, CSV, OSCAL)?
Read-only role + CSV/PDF export in v1; OSCAL later.
Does one run's evidence count toward all mapped frameworks immediately, or does someone confirm per framework?
Immediately at the mapped relation; customer can downgrade.
Retention defaults per regime (EU deployer logs >= 6 months, 42001 documented information) configurable per tenant?
Over-retention is a privacy risk; under-retention an audit risk.
Each connector is weeks of work and a support burden.
Okta/Entra, AWS IAM, GitHub, Jira/Linear, MLflow/SageMaker/Bedrock registry, OTel logs, HRIS, Google Drive/SharePoint, Slack/Teams approvals, LMS.
Approvals in Slack/Teams or only in-app?
Chat approvals raise identity binding and evidence capture questions.
Manual upload when no connector: accepted as evidence with a lower assurance label?
Without it, small customers cannot start.
MCP both ways: consume customer MCP servers as connectors, and expose a FairMind MCP server so customer agents can ask 'am I allowed to do X'?
The second is runtime policy enforcement: a different SLA.
Consume in v1; expose read-only policy lookup in v2.
Which agent platforms to discover first: Copilot Studio, Bedrock Agents, Vertex Agent Builder, LangGraph / custom via OTel?
Agent catalogue is empty without discovery.
OTel-based custom agents + Bedrock + Copilot Studio.
Govern only (record, review) or also enforce at runtime as a policy decision point?
Enforcement is a different product with latency and uptime promises.
Govern in v1; push policy to existing gateways rather than becoming one.
Agent identity source of truth: FairMind catalogue or the IdP's workload identities with FairMind as overlay?
IdP is source; FairMind adds owner, tier, capacity and evidence.
Adopt FairMind A0-A4 or align to SG MGF's four levels of human involvement exactly?
Customers will compare to the SG text.
Keep A0-A4 with a published mapping to SG levels.
Model multi-agent systems as one AI system with sub-agents, or separate records with a relationship graph?
Separate records + graph; system-level assessments at the parent.
Default rubber-stamp thresholds for override rate and review time?
SG MGF names the indicators but gives no values.
Flag override < 2% over 50 decisions, or median review < 10 s; tunable.

Content owner + 10 business days SLA for AIUC-1; 30 days for laws.
